body:
WHAT
Any Bash command that removes or destroys something (rm, del, rmdir, git clean, git push --force, git reset --hard, DROP TABLE, terraform destroy, find -delete, forced mv, …) always asks the user before it runs, in both permission stances, as long as the guard is on. Only an explicit literal grant for that exact command text (a subject-scoped allow rule, or an earlier 'always allow' on the same literal) or OVERDRIVE lets it skip the prompt. Turning off the guard (the 'Allow deletions' setting) makes deletions resolve through the normal rules.

WHY
Deleting is the irreversible action; without a target-shaped guard a frictionless 'commands run without asking' policy would let one bad command wipe user work.

WHERE
engine/tools/src/bash.ts — bashDeletionSubject() with DELETION_SINGLE_WORDS, DELETION_PHRASES, DELETION_PATTERN, GIT_BRANCH_FORCE_DELETE, GIT_CHECKOUT_DISCARD, FIND_DELETE, mvIsDestructive(); bashTool.deletionSubject. engine/core/src/runtime/permissions.ts — PermissionEngine.deletionGuard, setDeletionGuard(), check() deletion-guard block (explicitlyAllowed via matchesExplicit() / matchesExact(…, literalOnly=true), requestApproval(…, 'deletion-guard'), literal-only grantExact on allow_always). engine/core/src/runtime/session.ts — Session.setDeletionPolicy() flips the guard and the 'deletion-policy' prompt section.

TEST CHECKLIST
1. bashDeletionSubject returns the command for 'rm -rf build', 'git push --force', 'git reset --hard', 'DROP TABLE users', 'find . -name x -delete', 'mv -f a b', 'git branch -D foo'; and returns undefined for 'ls', 'mkdir x', 'npm run del-lint', 'git branch -d foo', 'mv a b'.
2. With the guard on and a broad allow rule 'Bash' (or session allow for the tool), PermissionEngine.check() for a Bash call whose deletionSubject is defined still calls requestApproval with source 'deletion-guard'.
3. A deny answer yields allowed:false with a message containing 'Deletion calls always require approval'.
4. An explicit subject rule 'Bash(rm -rf ./tmp/*)' in settings.allow lets the exact subject 'rm -rf ./tmp/*' run without prompting, while 'rm -rf ./src' still prompts.
5. After allow_always on a deletion prompt, the grant is literal: the identical command no longer prompts but 'rm -rf other' prompts again, and persistExact was called with prefix false.
6. setDeletionGuard(false) makes a non-protected deletion resolve as allowed:true, source:'mode' with no requestApproval call; setOverdrive(true) does the same even with the guard on.
